questions.q: The magnetic field inside a long, straight solenoid carrying current is ____________.
options: uniform and parallel to the axis of the solenoid
questions.solution:
Inside a long solenoid, the magnetic field is approximately uniform and runs parallel to the solenoid’s axis. End effects are small away from the ends.
**Answer: uniform and parallel to the axis of the solenoid**

questions.q: Which of the following materials is likely to be non-biodegradable?
questions.solution:
Conventional plastic does not break down readily through ordinary biological processes. Paper, wood and vegetable peels are biodegradable.
**Answer: Plastic**

questions.q: Which of the following articles deals with the Finance Commission that distributes taxes between the Centre and State?
questions.solution:
Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission. It recommends the sharing of tax proceeds and grants between the Union and states.
**Answer: Article 280**

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an agent of dispersal of seeds?
questions.solution:
Wind, water and animals can physically carry seeds to new locations. Sunlight supports plant growth but does not transport seeds.
**Answer: Sunlight**

questions.q: Self pollination is possible only in:
options: bisexual flowers with both stamens and pistil maturing at the different time
unisexual flowers with pistil maturing first
unisexual flowers with stamen maturing first
bisexual flowers with both stamens and pistil maturing at the same time
questions.solution:
Self-pollination requires the pollen and stigma to be available in the same flower or plant. Simultaneous maturation of stamens and pistil favours it.
**Answer: bisexual flowers with both stamens and pistil maturing at the same time**

questions.q: Where is the Taj Mahotsav held?
options: Near the Eastern gate of Taj Mahal
Near the Western gate of Taj Mahal
questions.solution:
Taj Mahotsav is organised at Shilpgram, near the eastern gate of the Taj Mahal in Agra.
**Answer: Near the Eastern gate of Taj Mahal**

questions.q: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was related to which of the following religious sects?
questions.solution:
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was a Vaishnava saint devoted to Krishna. He is closely associated with the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition.
**Answer: Vaishnava**

questions.q: Which of the following is a viral infection that can be transmitted through sexual contact?
questions.solution:
HIV is a virus and can be transmitted through sexual contact. Gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial infections.
**Answer: HIV-AIDS**

questions.q: Match the following rivers with their tributaries. Rivers Tributaries 1. Brahmaputra a. Betwa 2. Indus b. Chenab 3. Yamuna c. Dibang
questions.solution:
Dibang is a tributary of the Brahmaputra system, Chenab belongs to the Indus system, and Betwa joins the Yamuna. Hence 1-c, 2-b, 3-a.
**Answer: 1-c, 2-b, 3-a**

questions.q: What is the relationship between current (I), power (P), and voltage (V)?
questions.solution:
Electrical power is P = VI. Rearranging gives current I = P/V, so power divided by voltage is the required relation.
**Answer: I = P ÷ V**

questions.q: Which of the following articles deal with the provisions regarding the election, qualification, and removal of the Vice-President of India?
questions.solution:
Articles 63–71 cover the Vice-President and related election provisions. Article 63 establishes the office.
**Answer: Article 63 - 71**

questions.q: What is the process by which sodium hydroxide is prepared?
questions.solution:
The chlor-alkali process electrolyses brine. It produces sodium hydroxide, chlorine and hydrogen.
**Answer: Chlor-alkali process**

questions.q: In a series combination of resistors, how is the voltage distributed across each resistor?
questions.solution:
Series resistors carry the same current. Since V = IR, the voltage drop across each resistor is proportional to its resistance.
**Answer: Directly proportional to resistance**

questions.q: Which of the following is a method of reproduction in plants, where only a single parent is involved?
questions.solution:
Asexual reproduction involves one parent without fusion of male and female gametes. Plants can reproduce this way through vegetative propagation.
**Answer: Asexual reproduction**

questions.q: What determines the sex of a child in humans?
options: The temperature at which fertilised eggs are placed
questions.solution:
In humans, the sex-chromosome combination is the genetic basis of sex determination. Typically XX develops as female and XY as male.
**Answer: Genetic constitution**

questions.q: Every year, Foreign Trade Policy has been declared by which ministry of the Government of India?
questions.solution:
Foreign Trade Policy is administered by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry through the Directorate General of Foreign Trade. The policy is not necessarily renewed every calendar year.
**Answer: Ministry of Commerce and Industry**

questions.q: Who among the following is India's first civilian space tourist?
questions.solution:
Gopichand Thotakura travelled on Blue Origin’s NS-25 mission in May 2024, becoming India’s first civilian space tourist.
**Answer: Gopichand Thotakura**

questions.q: Which of the following is an effective method to reduce plastic waste?
questions.solution:
Reuse extends a plastic product’s life, while recycling recovers material for another use. Both reduce the amount discarded as waste.
**Answer: Recycling and reusing plastic materials**

questions.q: Which of the following is a natural ecosystem?
questions.solution:
A forest is a naturally occurring ecosystem. Crop fields, gardens and aquariums depend on deliberate human creation or management.
**Answer: Forest**

questions.q: Which of the following statements accurately describes the role of moral suasion in controlling money?
options: It is a combination of persuasion and pressure used by the RBI to influence banks' lending behaviour.
It is a direct tool used by the RBI to control the money supply by setting interest rates.
It refers to the variation in the statutory liquidity ratio to regulate the allocation of bank credit.
It involves the sale and purchase of government securities to influence the money supply.
questions.solution:
Moral suasion uses advice, persuasion and informal pressure to influence banks. It differs from compulsory reserve requirements or open-market transactions.
**Answer: It is a combination of persuasion and pressure used by the RBI to influence banks' lending behaviour.**

questions.q: What is the pH range of a strongly acidic solution?
questions.solution:
Strongly acidic solutions occupy the lower end of the pH scale. Among the listed intervals, 0–3 is the strongly acidic range.
**Answer: 0-3**

questions.q: Which of the following is the product of the neutralisation of hydrochloric acid (HCl) with sodium hydroxide (NaOH)?
questions.solution:
An acid and a base neutralise to form salt and water. Here HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O, producing sodium chloride and water.
**Answer: Sodium chloride and water**

questions.q: Which of the following released the fourth edition of SDG India Index 2023-24?
questions.solution:
NITI Aayog released the fourth SDG India Index, covering 2023–24. It tracks state and Union Territory progress on sustainable development goals.
**Answer: National Institute for Transforming India**

questions.q: Washing soda (Na 2 CO 3 ·10H 2 O) is obtained from which compound in the Solvay process?
questions.solution:
The Solvay process first precipitates sodium bicarbonate. Heating forms sodium carbonate, which can be crystallised with ten waters to make washing soda.
**Answer: Sodium bicarbonate**

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of an electric fuse in a household circuit?
options: To reduce resistance in the circuit
To prevent overloading and short circuits
questions.solution:
A fuse melts when excessive current flows and breaks the circuit. This protects wiring and appliances against overloads and short circuits.
**Answer: To prevent overloading and short circuits**

questions.q: What are regenerative cells used by Hydra for?
options: Hydra uses regenerative cells for reproduction by sexual reproduction.
Hydra uses regenerative cells for reproduction by spore formation.
Hydra uses regenerative cells for reproduction by fragmentation.
Hydra uses regenerative cells for reproduction by budding.
questions.solution:
Hydra commonly reproduces asexually by budding. Repeated cell division at one site produces a bud that develops into a new individual.
**Answer: Hydra uses regenerative cells for reproduction by budding.**

questions.q: The commutator in an electric motor is used to:
options: change the direction of the magnetic field
maintain the magnetic field in the circuit
maintain the potential difference in the circuit
reverse the direction of current flowing through the coil
questions.solution:
The split-ring commutator reverses current through the motor coil after each half-turn. This keeps the turning effect in the same rotational direction.
**Answer: reverse the direction of current flowing through the coil**

questions.q: What is the power rating of a device that draws 1.75 A of current when connected to a 180-V source?
questions.solution:
Power = voltage × current = 180 × 1.75 = 315 W.
**Answer: 315 W**

questions.q: Which of the following committees suggested that the 'duty to pay taxes' should also be a Fundamental Duty of the Indian citizen?
questions.solution:
The Swaran Singh Committee recommended adding Fundamental Duties and suggested a duty to pay taxes. That tax-duty proposal was not included in the enacted list.
**Answer: Swaran Singh Committee**

questions.q: Which of the following rules is used to determine the direction of the force on a current- carrying conductor in an electric motor?
questions.solution:
Fleming’s left-hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. It is the rule used for motor action.
**Answer: Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule**

questions.q: Which of the following countries hosted the first business summit of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) in 2024?
questions.solution:
The first BIMSTEC Business Summit was held in New Delhi in August 2024. India was the host country.
**Answer: New Delhi, India**

questions.q: Why is bleaching powder used for disinfecting drinking water?
options: It reduces the hardness of water.
It releases chlorine, which kills germs.
questions.solution:
Bleaching powder releases available chlorine. Chlorine acts as a disinfectant and kills many waterborne microorganisms.
**Answer: It releases chlorine, which kills germs.**

questions.q: The first session of Indian National Congress took place at which of the following places?
questions.solution:
The first Indian National Congress session was held in Bombay in December 1885. W. C. Bonnerjee presided over it.
**Answer: Bombay**

questions.q: The power in a circuit having voltage V and current I during time interval t is:
questions.solution:
Electrical power is P = VI. The time interval is relevant to energy, E = VIt, rather than to this expression for power.
**Answer: I × V**

questions.q: Who among the following secured a gold medal for India at the Paris Paralympics 2024?
questions.solution:
Avani Lekhara won gold in the women’s 10 m air-rifle standing SH1 event at the Paris 2024 Paralympics.
**Answer: Avani Lekhara**

questions.q: In a parallel circuit, how does the voltage across each resistor compare to the total voltage supplied by the battery?
options: It is the same for each resistor.
It is inversely proportional to the resistance.
It is divided according to the resistance values.
questions.solution:
Each parallel branch connects across the same two battery terminals. Hence every branch has the full supply voltage.
**Answer: It is the same for each resistor.**

questions.q: As of 30 September 2024, how many Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been established by the Government of India across the country?
questions.solution:
The dated count used in the paper is 13,822 Jan Aushadhi Kendras as of 30 September 2024. The date matters because the network expands over time.
**Answer: 13,822**

questions.q: An emf is induced whenever there is a change in the magnetic field linked with electric circuits. This is stated by the:
questions.solution:
Faraday’s law relates induced emf to the rate of change of magnetic flux through a circuit. Changing the linked field can therefore produce an emf.
**Answer: Faraday's law**

questions.q: If a child inherits an Y chromosome from the father, what will be the sex of the child?
questions.solution:
A Y chromosome from the father combines with the mother’s X chromosome to give XY, the usual male sex-chromosome combination.
**Answer: Male**
